summary: Lubefu territory (Sankuru) covers the Dikungu, Minga and Tshumbe secteurs, with Tshumbe (diocesan centre) as its largest town and Lubefu as territorial seat. It lies far from the eastern conflict zones and outside the core Kamuina Nsapu theatre; no armed group is known to hold territory as of 2026. Insecurity is mainly banditry, political tension and customary/land disputes. All locations are assessed as under ordinary state authority with the PNC as the main permanent force. Live web research was unavailable for this run, so confidence is medium for the towns and low for rural areas.

zones.description: Tshumbe (Tshumbe Mission / Dihokalenge agglomeration), Dikungu secteur
zones.evidence: Tshumbe is the largest town of Lubefu territory and seat of the Catholic diocese, with a PNC presence, courts and territorial services; no armed group is known to hold or tax it. Insecurity is limited to banditry and political/customary tensions. zones.description: Rural villages of Dikungu, Minga and Tshumbe secteurs (Minga, Tshumbe, Wembo Nyama, Pania Mutombo and Tshofa health zones)
zones.evidence: No organised armed group is known to control villages in Lubefu territory; the Kamuina Nsapu insurgency of 2016-2017 did not establish control here and has ended. Order rests on thin PNC posts, customary chiefs and the territorial administration; local insecurity consists of banditry and land/chieftaincy disputes.
